Here's a starting framework. Exact numbers depend on age, sex, and activity level, which would help me refine this.

**Key note:** At 165 cm and 95 kg, BMI is about 35. For someone at this weight, "lean gain" usually works best as a small calorie surplus or a body recomposition approach (building muscle while losing some fat). Some people in this situation do better with a modest deficit first. A doctor or registered dietitian can help set the right approach.

## Daily Targets (estimates)

- **Calories:** roughly 2,300-2,600 kcal (maintenance is probably around 2,200-2,500; add about 200-300 for a slow surplus)
- **Protein:** 140-170 g/day (about 1.6-2 g per kg of goal body weight, which keeps it high without overdoing it)
- **Carbs:** 250-300 g/day, focused around training
- **Fat:** 70-85 g/day, mostly unsaturated
- **Fiber:** 30+ g/day
- **Water:** about 3 liters/day, more if active

## Gluten-Free Food Choices

- **Protein:** chicken, turkey, lean beef, eggs, salmon, tuna, shrimp, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, tofu, tempeh, lentils, beans (check processed meats and sauces for hidden gluten)
- **Carbs:** rice, potatoes, sweet potatoes, quinoa, buckwheat, corn tortillas, certified gluten-free oats, fruit, rice cakes
- **Fats:** olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, nut butters, fatty fish
- **Vegetables:** almost all, especially leafy greens, broccoli, peppers, carrots, and berries for micronutrients

Avoid wheat, barley, rye, and malt. Watch for gluten in soy sauce (use tamari), seasonings, sauces, and beer.

## Sample Day (~2,400 kcal, ~160 g protein)

- **Breakfast:** 3 eggs + 1 cup egg whites scrambled with spinach, 1 cup berries, 1/2 cup GF oats cooked in milk with a tablespoon of peanut butter
- **Snack:** 1 cup Greek yogurt, a handful of almonds, banana
- **Lunch:** 150 g grilled chicken, 1 cup cooked rice, roasted vegetables, olive oil dressing
- **Pre-workout:** rice cakes with turkey or a banana with a scoop of whey (GF-labeled)
- **Post-workout/Dinner:** 170 g salmon or lean beef, 1 large baked potato with Greek yogurt, big salad with avocado
- **Evening snack:** cottage cheese with honey and berries

## Training and Recovery Tips

- Lift weights 3-5 times per week, progressively increasing load.
- Prioritize sleep (7-9 hours); muscle growth happens during recovery.
- Track your weight and waist measurements weekly. Aim for about 0.25-0.5 kg of gain per month if the goal is lean muscle. Faster gain usually means more fat.
- Adjust calories by 100-150 kcal every 2-3 weeks based on progress.

If you share your age, sex, activity level, and training schedule, I can tailor the calorie and macro numbers more precisely.

Here's a practical starting point. It's based on the numbers you gave, and I've assumed an adult with light to moderate activity.

## Snapshot
- **BMI:** about 20.0, within the healthy range
- **Estimated maintenance calories:** roughly 1,700–1,900 kcal/day. Adjust by 100–200 kcal based on whether their weight holds steady over 2–3 weeks.
- **Protein:** about 45–55 g/day (roughly 1 g per kg of body weight). This supports muscle maintenance, which helps joint health and movement quality.
- **Carbs:** about 45–55% of calories, prioritizing whole grains, fruit, and starchy vegetables for energy around stretching or training.
- **Fat:** about 25–30% of calories, emphasizing omega-3s and unsaturated fats.

Flexibility depends mostly on consistent stretching, strength training through a full range of motion, sleep, and hydration. Diet supports this by keeping muscles and connective tissue well fueled and healthy. No specific food will make someone more flexible on its own.

## Nutrients to Prioritize
- **Protein:** tofu, tempeh, edamame, lentils, beans, chickpeas, eggs, fish, chicken, lean meat, quinoa
- **Calcium (no dairy):** fortified soy milk, calcium-set tofu, bok choy, kale, collard greens, broccoli, tahini, sesame seeds, chia seeds, fortified oat or rice milk
- **Vitamin C (for collagen synthesis):** citrus, kiwi, strawberries, bell peppers, tomatoes, broccoli
- **Magnesium (muscle function):** pumpkin seeds, spinach, black beans, whole grains, dark chocolate
- **Omega-3s:** salmon, sardines, mackerel, flaxseed, chia, walnuts are out (nut-free), so use seeds and fish
- **Iron:** lean red meat, lentils, tofu, fortified cereals, spinach, paired with vitamin C
- **Vitamin D:** fatty fish, eggs, fortified soy or oat milk; consider a supplement if sunlight is limited (check with a doctor)

## Sample Day (~1,800 kcal, ~50 g protein)
- **Breakfast:** Oatmeal made with fortified soy milk, topped with strawberries, chia seeds, and a spoonful of tahini or sunflower seed butter (about 400 kcal)
- **Snack:** Orange and a small handful of pumpkin seeds (about 180 kcal)
- **Lunch:** Quinoa bowl with baked tofu, roasted broccoli and bell peppers, edamame, and lemon-tahini dressing (about 550 kcal)
- **Snack:** Hummus (chickpea-based) with carrot and cucumber sticks (about 200 kcal)
- **Dinner:** Baked salmon, sweet potato, sautéed spinach or bok choy with garlic and olive oil (about 500 kcal)
- **Optional:** Kiwi or berries with a small dark chocolate square (about 100 kcal)

## Practical Tips
- **Read labels carefully.** Many "dairy-free" products contain nuts, and many "nut-free" products are made in facilities that process nuts. If the allergy is severe, look for "may contain" warnings and choose certified nut-free products.
- **Watch for hidden dairy:** whey, casein, butter, ghee, and some baked goods, breads, and processed snacks.
- **Hydrate:** roughly 2–2.5 liters of water a day, more if active.
- **Eat regularly:** three meals plus one or two snacks helps maintain energy and weight.
- **Track trends, not single days.** Weigh weekly and adjust portions if weight drifts more than about 1 kg in either direction over a month.

If this person has a medical condition, takes medications, is very active, or has a history of disordered eating, a registered dietitian can tailor these numbers. If you share age, sex, and activity level, I can refine the calorie and protein targets.

# Vegan Marathon Training Meal Plan

**Estimated targets** (assuming an adult male, moderate-to-high training volume, about 50-70 km/week):

| Target | Daily Goal | Approx. Per kg |
|---|---|---|
| Calories | ~3,000 kcal | ~43 kcal/kg |
| Carbohydrates | ~420-480 g | ~6-7 g/kg |
| Protein | ~130-150 g | ~1.9-2.1 g/kg |
| Fat | ~80-90 g | ~1.2 g/kg |

Adjust calories up or down by 200-300 kcal based on weight trends. Aim for steady weight, or a slight loss of no more than 0.5 kg/week during peak training.

## Sample Day (~3,000 kcal, ~150 g protein, ~415 g carbs, ~85 g fat)

**Breakfast: Banana-Oat Power Bowl** (~720 kcal)
- 80 g dry rolled oats, cooked in 350 ml fortified soy milk
- 1 large banana, sliced
- 2 tbsp maple syrup
- 20 g hemp seeds

**Lunch: Tempeh & Chickpea Grain Bowl** (~820 kcal)
- 150 g tempeh, pan-fried or baked
- 250 g cooked brown rice
- 100 g roasted chickpeas and vegetables (sweet potato, peppers, zucchini)
- 1 tbsp tahini-lemon dressing

**Afternoon Snack: Recovery Smoothie** (~275 kcal)
- 300 ml fortified soy milk
- 1 scoop pea or soy protein powder (~25-30 g)
- 150 g frozen berries

**Dinner: Lentil Bolognese with Whole Wheat Pasta** (~905 kcal)
- 120 g dry whole wheat pasta
- 150 g cooked red lentils, simmered in tomato sauce
- 200 g marinara sauce, with 1 tbsp olive oil
- 100 g edamame on the side

**Evening Snack: Peanut Butter Toast** (~300 kcal)
- 2 slices whole grain bread
- 1 tbsp peanut butter
- Fruit or a glass of soy milk

## Adjusting for Training

- **Long-run and hard-session days:** Add 100-150 g carbs. Extra rice, bread, potatoes, fruit, or a sports drink works well.
- **Rest days:** Reduce carbs slightly and keep protein steady.
- **Pre-run (1-3 hours before):** Eat easily digestible carbs such as toast with jam, a banana, or rice cakes, with little fat or fiber.
- **During runs over 60-90 minutes:** Take 30-60 g carbs per hour from gels, dates, maple syrup packets, or sports drinks. Practice this in training, not on race day.
- **Post-run (within 60 minutes):** Have a carb-protein combination, such as a smoothie with soy milk, protein powder, and fruit.

## Protein Sources to Rotate

- Tofu, tempeh, seitan
- Lentils, chickpeas, black beans, split peas
- Soy milk, soy yogurt, edamame
- Pea or soy protein powder
- Quinoa, oats, hemp seeds, chia seeds, pumpkin seeds

## Nutrients to Watch

Vegan athletes are more likely to fall short on these, so consider:

- **Vitamin B12:** Supplement daily (25-100 mcg) or use fortified foods. This is essential.
- **Iron:** Pair plant iron (lentils, tofu, spinach, fortified cereals) with vitamin C foods like peppers, citrus, or tomatoes. Iron status is worth checking with a doctor, especially for endurance athletes.
- **Calcium:** Use fortified soy milk, calcium-set tofu, tahini, and leafy greens.
- **Omega-3s:** Include ground flaxseed, chia, walnuts, or an algae-based DHA/EPA supplement.
- **Vitamin D and iodine:** Consider supplements, especially in low-sunlight months. Iodized salt or seaweed also helps.
- **Zinc:** Good
